genre/modale-jazz: Improvising on scales (modes) instead of fast chord changes
Improvisation on scales (modes) instead of rapidly changing chords.
genre/nederbeat: Dutch beat music of the 1960s, mostly in English
genre/nederpop: Dutch pop music, mostly in the Dutch language
genre/nouvelle-vague: French 'new wave' of young critic-directors from the late 1950s.
genre/nu-jazz: Hybrid of jazz and electronic dance music, with samples, beats and live instruments.
genre/ragtime: Written-out piano music with a syncopated melody over a steady left hand.
genre/skiffle: British do-it-yourself music with washboard and tea-chest bass (1950s)
genre/soul: Gospel and rhythm and blues with secular lyrics
genre/spaghettiwestern: Italian Western, often filmed in Spain, cheaper and harder-edged than the American kind.
genre/synthwave: Music from around 2010 that imitates the synthesizer sound of the 1980s.
genre/third-stream: Schuller's term (1957) for music that joins jazz and European concert music.
techniek/auto-tune: Software that corrects pitch, also used as an effect
techniek/midi: Standard that lets instruments and computers exchange notes
Standard (1983) that lets instruments and computers communicate
techniek/theremin: Electronic instrument you play by moving your hands in an electric field, without touching it.
Electronic instrument you play without touching it, with gliding tones.
techniek/vocoder: Device that lays the tone colour of a voice onto a synthesizer
Device that makes a voice sound like a synthesizer.
Device that transfers the tone colour of a voice onto a synthesizer, so that the synthesizer seems to sing.
techniek/wall-of-sound: Phil Spector's production style, with doubled instruments and reverb
